clue.text: She could be trusted to cheat if turned poet

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat or swindle them

indicators.note: turned asks for the little word if to be written back to front

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A woman of trust might be tempted into fraud if she took up verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes FI from 'if', sitting between CON and DANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in whom secrets are placed is a trusted female intimate.

clue.text: Some pop a question that's "not clear

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Proposing marriage can leave things murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something murky lets no light through and so is hard to see into or understand.

clue.text: Complaisant when troubles befell about the team

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the team, which sits inside them
troubles means the letters of befell are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: XI, Roman eleven, is the usual shorthand for a side such as a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Someone stays agreeable when misfortunes strike the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' rearranges BEFELL into FLEBLE, and 'about' wraps that round XI.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaisant person is accommodating and willing to bend to others' wishes.

clue.text: Sewers of trousers ?

explanation.surface: Do sewers make trousers? A seamstress pun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' reads as people who sew, but here it means drains; skinny trousers of the 1950s were also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewers are waste pipes for drainage; very narrow-legged trousers worn by Teddy boys share the name.

clue.text: Job for a trawler in broadcasting organization

explanation.surface: A fisherman's task turns up inside a television company.
explanation.definitionFit: A trawlerman's task is working the nets; a chain of linked radio or TV stations shares the name.

clue.text: John Welsh causes retreat of Church body

indicators.note: a retreat is a backward movement, so the word for the church body is read in reverse

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church, where the congregation sits

explanation.surface: A Welshman called John makes a congregation withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat of' turns NAVE round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Welsh form of the name John.

clue.text: Doubly appropriate for a gin-drinking king ?

definitions.text: Doubly appropriate for a gin-drinking king ?

parts.words: Doubly appropriate for a gin-drinking king ?
parts.note: a king lives in a palace, and a drinker cares for his palate, so the word fits both sides of him

explanation.surface: A tippling monarch is suited twice over by one adjective.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as PALATI-AL, fit for the palate, while its plain sense is fit for a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and splendid like a royal residence, with a nod to the drinker's sense of taste.

clue.text: Pollen's the trouble in the old Dardanelles

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of pollen's and the are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: the word is taken with its S as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Hay fever strikes in the strait between Europe and Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges POLLENS and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellespont is the ancient Greek name of the Dardanelles strait in Turkey.

clue.text: Caveat reissued to give up possession

indicators.note: reissued suggests the word caveat being put out again in a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A legal warning is republished to make someone surrender a property.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a house is to leave it and give up occupancy.

clue.text: Catch an Oriental returning in the title-role

indicators.note: returning says the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: to trap is to catch
an eastern man: E for east plus MAN

explanation.surface: An actor nabs an Asian visitor on his way back while playing the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TRAP + E + MAN round to read NAME PART.
explanation.definitionFit: The name part is the role that gives a play its name, as Hamlet in Hamlet.

clue.text: Lull in the storm that's unexpectedly beneficial ?

definitions.text: Lull in the storm that's unexpectedly beneficial ?

parts.words: Lull in the storm that's unexpectedly beneficial ?
parts.note: a drop in the gale reads literally as the ..., but the phrase means a stroke of unearned luck

explanation.surface: A quiet moment in bad weather turns out to be a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: Originally the word meant fruit blown down by the wind, free for the taking.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected gain, such as a legacy or bonus, that comes as a piece of luck.

clue.text: The lady's note is simple

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman, the lady's
B is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A woman's message is easy to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' is a noun here: an old word for a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is a plant used in folk medicine, a single-ingredient remedy.

clue.text: Piece polished up by the cavalry band ?

definitions.text: Piece polished up by the cavalry band ?

parts.words: Piece polished up by the cavalry band ?
parts.note: a mounted band's instruments would be literally brass for horses, and the brass harness ornament is polished up

explanation.surface: A musical piece is rehearsed to perfection by the mounted regiment's musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests music to be polished, but it is a metal medallion worn on a horse's harness.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass ornament fixed to a draught animal's harness, shined up for shows.

clue.text: Security covers harbour-leaves

parts.note: a port is a harbour
folios are leaves or sheets of a book

explanation.surface: An insurance policy covers the dockside foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security' is a stocks-and-shares sense: the cases hold an investor's securities or papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat cases for carrying documents, and also an investor's collection of shares.

clue.text: Bond in action with learned opponents ?

definitions.text: Bond in action with learned opponents ?

parts.words: Bond in action with learned opponents ?
parts.note: in a court action, opposing barristers call each other my learned friend, so their bond would be a close tie between pals

explanation.surface: A legal bond is tested in a lawsuit against clever rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts counsel refer to the opposing barrister as 'my learned friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond of affection between companions.

clue.text: Put paid to instruction for course preparation

explanation.surface: Someone ended a cookery lesson for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put paid to' sounds like 'end', but here it means to mark a bill as settled; 'course' is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark a bill as settled with a signed note; an old word for a recipe.

clue.text: The tooth it swallowed makes us think

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
ate means swallowed, consumed

explanation.surface: Biting down on something gets the brain going.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or reflect deeply on a matter.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman concealed a damaging log

parts.note: hid means concealed

indicators.note: damaging suggests a and log being knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman covered up the harm done to a ship's record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging' rearranges A and LOG into ALGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lower Spanish nobility.

clue.text: Ceremonial interview for playgoers

explanation.surface: Theatregoers granted a formal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal meeting with a monarch or pope; also the spectators at a play.

clue.text: Issue can mean tea redistribution

indicators.note: redistribution says the letters of mean and tea are shared out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Handing out tea from a pot could cause a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link; 'redistribution' rearranges MEAN and TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow out or come forth from a source.

clue.text: Wellington was the last great one, said Tennyson .

definitions.text: Wellington was the last great one, said Tennyson .

parts.words: Wellington was the last great one, said Tennyson .
parts.note: Tennyson's Ode on the Death of the Duke of Wellington calls the Duke the last great man of his nation

explanation.surface: A quotation from Tennyson about the Duke of Wellington.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'The last great Englishman is low', from Tennyson's 1852 ode.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from England, as Tennyson described the Duke.

clue.text: Not much money so act

explanation.surface: Short of cash, get on with it!
explanation.walkthrough: A doit was a small old Dutch coin, so a trifling sum; split, the letters say 'do it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny old coin, hence a trifle; the phrase urging someone to act.

clue.text: Contract place for new recruits

explanation.surface: An agreement signs up fresh soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is a noun on the surface but here means a narrowing; an intake is also the point where new members are taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowing in a pipe or garment; the batch or point of entry of new trainees.

clue.text: A scheme to pursue the renegade with drum-beats

indicators.note: to pursue means to follow behind, so these pieces come after the renegade

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or turncoat
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A plan to chase down a traitor to the sound of drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pursue' puts A PLAN after RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rataplan is the rhythmic sound of a drum being beaten.

clue.text: Many decision-makers

explanation.surface: Plenty of people make the choices.
explanation.definitionFit: A great number of things; straws or tokens drawn to settle a choice by chance.

clue.text: Greek to a one-time Scot

explanation.surface: Something is Greek to a Scot of former times.
explanation.walkthrough: Edinburgh was nicknamed the Athens of the North, so its citizens were once called Modern Athenians.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Athens; a nineteenth-century nickname for a resident of Edinburgh.

clue.text: Seems as if all in France take no part in the dance

definitions.text: take no part in the dance

parts.note: si is French for if
tout is French for all

explanation.surface: A wallflower seems to sit apart while everyone in France dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' tells the solver to give 'if' and 'all' in French; 'Seems as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out a dance is to stay seated and not join in.

clue.text: Amorous looks of those on the run?

definitions.text: Amorous looks of those on the run?

parts.words: Amorous looks of those on the run?
parts.note: a sheep run is a pasture, so the flock on it would have the eyes of its animals, the phrase for lovesick glances

explanation.surface: Fugitives cast longing glances at each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the run' suggests fugitives, but a run is grazing land for a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting, lovesick glances given by a besotted admirer.
